newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL joins TCPL-led Sable pipeline project.
newsitem.headline: IPL joins TCPL-led Sable pipeline project.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc said on Monday it entered the battle over building pipeline capacity from the proposed Sable natural gas project off Canada's east coast by signing on with the group led by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd.
IPL said it would pay a third of the TransMaritime Gas Transmission project's C$665 million capital cost through its wholly owned Ontario gas utility, Consumers Gas.
The other TransMaritime partner is Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP.

The pipeline would ship the Sable project's 500 million cubic feet a day of gas to the Trans Quebec & Maritimes pipeline in Quebec -- part of TransCanada's existing cross-Canada mainline system -- from Goldboro, Nova Scotia.
The gas would then be shipped to U.S. Northeast markets on the proposed Portland Natural Gas Transmission line.
The project is in competition with the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, which would also ship Sable gas to the U.S. Northeast via Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, but bypass Quebec.
Main partners in the C$1 billion Maritimes & Northeast project include Mobil Corp, unit Mobil Oil Canada, Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp.

Consumers Gas Chief Operating Officer Ron Munkley said his firm's decision to invest in the TMGT proposal followed an extensive review of costs, toll design and the competing plan for moving Sable Island gas.
"Based on our assessment, this project is the best alternative for transporting Sable Island gas to market," Munkley said in a statement.

"It provides the lowest toll to Maritime markets, better access to New Brunswick communities and competitive tolls to those proposed by Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline project for the U.S. northeast. We also expect that it can be in place at least as quickly as any alternative," he said.

He also said it fit with Consumers' own plans to develop gas distribution in Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as well as bring Sable gas into Ontario without affecting tolls currently paid by TransCanada shippers.

Issues over which firms should build the pipeline to carry Sable gas, and the route it should follow, is politically charged, with Quebec separatist Premier Lucien Bouchard supporting the TransCanada-led plan and Nova Scotia Premier John Savage backing Maritimes & Northeast.
TransCanada has conceded it was behind Maritimes & Northeast in the race to build pipeline capacity from Sable.

Earlier, its project was delayed by negotiations in which it had to convince Quebec regulators and Gaz Metro that western Canadian shippers could not be charged more than east coast shippers to use the system.
It plans to make its full filing with Canada's National Energy Board by the end of the summer.
